official_sources.title: NIST Type A evaluation of standard uncertainty
official_sources.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology
official_sources.finding: Type A standard uncertainty is evaluated by statistical analysis of a series of observations; repeated-observation dispersion and uncertainty of the mean must remain tied to the actual sample design and degrees of freedom.
official_sources.limitation: Repeatability statistics do not include unobserved systematic effects, datum errors, raster lineage errors or spatial correlation unless modeled.

official_sources.title: NIST Type B evaluation of standard uncertainty
official_sources.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology
official_sources.finding: Type B evaluation uses scientific judgment based on all available information, including prior measurements, specifications, calibration data and reference information, and converts the assumed distribution into a standard uncertainty.
official_sources.limitation: A Type B estimate is only as defensible as its evidence, distribution, bounds and independence assumptions.

official_sources.title: NIST combined standard uncertainty
official_sources.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology
official_sources.finding: Combined standard uncertainty represents the estimated standard deviation of the result and combines Type A and Type B components using propagation of uncertainty, including covariances where appropriate; recognized systematic effects should be corrected rather than hidden inside random error.
official_sources.limitation: Simple root-sum-of-squares is invalid when covariance, nonlinear response or omitted systematic effects are material.

official_sources.title: NIST law of propagation of uncertainty
official_sources.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology
official_sources.finding: The propagation law uses sensitivity coefficients, component variances and covariance terms under a first-order Taylor approximation; the measurement function must include all quantities that contribute significant uncertainty.
official_sources.limitation: The first-order approximation requires validation when transformations, extrema selection, clipping or other operations are nonlinear.

official_sources.title: NIST expanded uncertainty and coverage factor
official_sources.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology
official_sources.finding: Expanded uncertainty is U = k times the combined standard uncertainty; the coverage factor and associated confidence interpretation depend on distributional assumptions, with k near 2 giving approximately 95 percent coverage only under stated conditions.
official_sources.limitation: A fixed k cannot be used without documenting degrees of freedom, distribution assumptions and the intended coverage probability.

official_sources.title: NIST uncertainty reporting requirements
official_sources.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology
official_sources.finding: Reports should state combined or expanded uncertainty, the coverage factor, all uncertainty components, how each component was evaluated and the basis of any confidence interpretation.
official_sources.limitation: A well-formatted uncertainty statement does not compensate for missing components, invalid assumptions or absent source measurements.

official_sources.title: USGS lidar accuracy, RMSE and RMSD definitions
official_sources.finding: USGS distinguishes absolute accuracy from relative precision, RMSE from an independent higher-accuracy reference, and RMSD between datasets when neither is known to be more accurate; vertical accuracy is tied to a specified vertical datum and confidence or percentile statement.
official_sources.limitation: Project-level RMSE or accuracy class does not prove the error of a specific parcel pixel or extrema pair.

official_sources.title: USGS 3DEP lidar vertical accuracy requirements
official_sources.finding: The current 3DEP lidar specification requires absolute and relative vertical accuracy validation and detailed reporting; NVA and VVA are assessed separately, and survey error is included when calculating RMSEv for NVA.
official_sources.limitation: A dataset specification or class is a prior constraint and cannot replace parcel-specific valid-support execution and uncertainty propagation.
